questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Critical angle from glass to air
questions.learningObjective: Justify why the critical angle marks the boundary of total internal reflection
questions.stem: Ticket GL-104 asks why a ray in crown glass of index 1.52 meeting a glass-air boundary at 41 degrees still refracts into air, while a ray at 42 degrees is trapped inside the glass.

options.text: The 42 degree ray is reflected because a glass surface behaves like a mirror at grazing angles
options.misconception: believes any steeply incident ray reflects off the surface

options.text: The 41 degree ray has exactly grazed the surface, so it is reflected at the glass boundary
options.misconception: confuses the critical angle with a grazing incidence

options.text: The 41 degree ray is below the 41.1 degree critical angle, so it refracts into the air
Light inside glass travels faster than in air, so refraction at the boundary reverses direction
options.misconception: believes light speeds up when entering the rarer medium

questions.explanation: The critical angle for crown glass is arcsin(1/1.52) = 41.1 degrees, so a 41 degree incidence is below it and refracts out. Above that angle no refracted ray exists and the ray is totally internally reflected.
questions.hint: Compare the incidence angle with arcsin of 1 over n.

questions.topic: Condition required for total internal reflection

options.text: The incident ray must travel in the denser medium and strike the boundary beyond the critical angle
options.misconception: treats the denser medium as the rarer side of the boundary

options.text: Light must move from a higher index to a lower index medium at an angle greater than the critical angle
The incident ray must arrive perpendicular to the boundary so that it cannot bend away from the normal
options.misconception: believes normal incidence causes internal reflection

options.text: The two media must have equal indices so that the refracted ray grazes the boundary
options.misconception: confuses a vanishing refracted ray with equal indices

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection needs light going from denser to rarer medium and striking beyond the critical angle, where no refracted ray exists. Equal indices never bend the ray and normal incidence is the safest case.
questions.hint: Denser to rarer, and beyond the critical angle.

options.misconception: believes a large index prevents a critical angle

options.misconception: mistakes partial reflection for total internal reflection

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection starts at the critical angle, so bracketing it between 24 and 25 degrees gives a value near 24.5 degrees. The calculation arcsin(1/2.42) = 24.4 degrees confirms this.

The solid at 41.8 degrees is diamond and the one at 19.5 degrees is a solid denser than diamond

questions.explanation: Ranking by index is ranking by inverse critical angle: diamond at 2.42 gives 24.4 degrees, glass at 1.5 gives 41.8 degrees and water at 1.33 gives 48.8 degrees.
questions.hint: A higher index always gives a smaller critical angle.

questions.explanation: At twice the focal length the object and image distances are equal, so the diagram must show the inverted equal-size image at 2F on the opposite side. Any other mark contradicts the lens equation.
questions.hint: Object at 2F, image at 2F, same size, inverted.
